title: Runtime-named rerun outputs search for a noncanonical pipeline-sidecar filename
observed_behavior: When the backend gives a TV output a runtime-only episode title, reconciliation scans sibling media but looks for '<media filename including extension>.pipeline.json'. The canonical helper used by production publish/evidence code creates '<media basename>.pipeline.json', so a valid runtime-named output and canonical sidecar are rejected as RERUN_OUTPUT_EVIDENCE_MISSING.
expected_invariant: Runtime-named reconciliation must use the same canonical sidecar-path contract as every other rerun evidence reader and must accept exactly one identity-matched, stage-matched output without weakening ambiguity checks.
root_cause: Resolve-RerunProducedOutput hand-builds the sidecar path by appending '.pipeline.json' to candidate.FullName instead of calling Get-RerunPipelineSidecarPath.
failure_scenario: TV planning expects 'Show - S00E01.mkv', runtime naming produces 'Show - S00E01 - Episode Title.mkv' and its canonical 'Show - S00E01 - Episode Title.pipeline.json'. The planned file is absent, the scan never opens the canonical sidecar, and the verified output remains in review instead of being reconciled and published.
evidence: planning.ps1 line 585 constructs "$($candidate.FullName).pipeline.json" while evidence.ps1 lines 50-54 removes the media extension before adding .pipeline.json.
A current synthetic fixture containing the actual media and canonical sidecar returned Path='' and Code='RERUN_OUTPUT_EVIDENCE_MISSING'.
Invoke-RerunPlanOnlyChecks.ps1 lines 106-128 creates '<actual>.mkv.pipeline.json', so its passing reconciliation assertion exercises the noncanonical name and masks the production mismatch.
affected_flows: CSV rerun TV outputs whose runtime naming adds an episode title
existing_safeguards: Reconciliation requires exactly one candidate with matching source_identity_v2, stage source_path, and sidecar output_path.
Ambiguous and incomplete evidence fails closed without changing source media.
safeguard_gap: The identity checks are sound only after the sidecar is found; the filename mismatch prevents canonical evidence from reaching them, and the focused test duplicates the same wrong construction.
tests_present: ops/pipeline/tests/Unit/Invoke-RerunPlanOnlyChecks.ps1 covers runtime-named reconciliation and ambiguity but builds noncanonical sidecar names.
tests_missing: Assertion that all rerun sidecar consumers call the canonical path helper
End-to-end runtime TV naming rerun through verified publication
recommended_remediation: Replace the manual append with Get-RerunPipelineSidecarPath -OutputPath $candidate.FullName, update the reconciliation fixtures to canonical sidecar names, and retain all current identity, stage-path, output-path, and ambiguity checks.
remediation_risk: Low-to-medium: the path correction is narrow, but tests should decide whether legacy extension-bearing sidecars need read-only compatibility without creating a second authoritative convention.
validation_rung: Focused RerunPlanOnly checks with canonical and legacy-negative fixtures, rerun source-identity checks, and a synthetic TV runtime-naming publish flow; representative real media is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: No current finding with this canonical-sidecar filename root cause was present in the assembled finding fragments; reproduced against the exact current hash.

title: publish_non_overlap moves only media and strands every companion artifact
observed_behavior: The publish_non_overlap branch moves the verified media to its final non-overlapping destination and marks the plan published, but never invokes the companion publisher. The pipeline sidecar, converted SRT files, and completed-jobs mirror remain at the verified-output workspace.
expected_invariant: Every successful final-library publication mode must commit the media and its canonical pipeline sidecar, declared subtitle sidecars, and completion evidence as one recoverable publication outcome.
root_cause: Companion publication is implemented inside Publish-RerunPipelineSidecarToFinal and called by replace-final only; the separate non-overlap branch calls only Move-RerunVerifiedOutput before declaring success.
failure_scenario: An operator selects publish_non_overlap for a verified rerun with a pipeline sidecar and generated SRT. The final media appears and the row reports published_non_overlap, but no final sidecar or SRT exists and no completed-jobs entry records the publication.
evidence: publish.ps1 lines 536-548 contains no call to Publish-RerunPipelineSidecarToFinal; replace-final calls it at line 462.

A current isolated synthetic run returned Status='published_non_overlap', PublishedMediaExists=true, PublishedSidecarExists=false, PublishedSrtExists=false, SourceSidecarStranded=true, SourceSrtStranded=true, and CompletedManifestExists=false.
The branch invokes original-file policy after the media-only move, so the success state is externally visible rather than a pre-publication preview.
affected_flows: pipeline-sidecar provenance in the final library
existing_safeguards: Media destination collisions are either failed or given a non-overlap suffix.
Verified output is moved through the bounded rerun move helper.
Replace-final and pending-publish modes have explicit companion-evidence handling.
safeguard_gap: There is no branch-local companion commit, rollback, or postcondition requiring final sidecar/subtitle/completion evidence before success.
tests_present: Rerun recovery tests recognize published_non_overlap as a terminal state; focused rerun checks passed but do not assert companion artifacts for this branch.
tests_missing: publish_non_overlap fixture with canonical pipeline sidecar, one converted SRT, and completed-jobs manifest assertions
Fault injection between media and companion publication
Recovery test for a partially committed non-overlap publication
recommended_remediation: Route non-overlap through a shared transactional final-publication helper that publishes media plus all declared companions, appends completion evidence, verifies postconditions, and rolls back or records an explicit recoverable partial state on failure.
remediation_risk: High: changing final publication ordering can strand or overwrite evidence if rollback and collision paths are incomplete. Preserve non-overlap naming and never mutate source media.
validation_rung: Rerun destination/recovery unit tests, transactional fault injection at each media/sidecar/SRT/manifest boundary, pending-publish parity checks, and representative subtitle-sidecar publication evidence before release.
prior_audit_relationship: No assembled current finding covered the media-only publish_non_overlap branch; reproduced against the exact current hash with an isolated filesystem fixture.

title: Replace-final commits new media before companion evidence and has no rollback on sidecar failure
observed_behavior: Replace-final first moves the old final media into hold and moves the new media into the final path. Only afterward does it copy SRTs, back up companions, write the canonical sidecar, and append completion evidence. Any companion exception reaches the outer destination-policy catch, which labels the plan failed without restoring either media move.
expected_invariant: A final replacement must be atomic or explicitly recoverable: it may report published only after media and required evidence commit, and any pre-commit failure must restore the prior final state or durably record a partial transaction for deterministic recovery.
root_cause: The media replacement and companion publication are sequential destructive moves without a transaction boundary, rollback handler, or durable intermediate lifecycle state.
failure_scenario: The old final is moved to hold and the verified media becomes the final file; writing the destination pipeline sidecar then fails. The plan says failed, the new media remains final, the old media remains in hold, and the verified workspace no longer contains the media, so a retry cannot safely infer or repeat the operation.
evidence: Publish-RerunReplaceFinal lines 453-461 backs up old media and moves new media before line 462 calls the companion publisher.
Publish-RerunPipelineSidecarToFinal lines 220-235 performs SRT copies, companion backups, sidecar write, and completion append after the media move.
Invoke-RerunDestinationPolicy lines 561-564 catches the exception only by setting status='failed' and logging the reason.

A current isolated fault fixture made the destination sidecar path a directory; after bounded write retries, Status='failed', final bytes were 'new-media', the hold backup bytes were 'old-media', VerifiedStillExists=false, and no sidecar file existed.
affected_flows: final media and companion evidence consistency
rerun retry and recovery after partial publication
existing_safeguards: Old final media and existing companions are placed under the batch hold root.
Sidecar writes are bounded and errors surface to the plan.
safeguard_gap: Backups make manual recovery possible but do not make the operation atomic; failure is misrepresented as an unapplied plan and no code restores backups or records a recoverable partial-commit state.
tests_present: Rerun auto-destination and recovery suites cover successful and policy-routing behavior but no companion-write failure after the media move was found.
tests_missing: Fault injection after old-media backup, after new-media move, during each SRT copy, during sidecar write, and during completion append
Restart recovery from each partial transaction state
Assertion that a failed replacement leaves the original final fully restored
recommended_remediation: Introduce a manifest-backed replacement transaction with explicit prepared, media_staged, companions_staged, committed, and rollback-required states. Stage new media/companions to same-volume temporary paths, verify them, atomically commit in a defined order, and restore the held final plus companions on any pre-commit failure.
remediation_risk: High: final-library replacement, cross-volume behavior, collision handling, and subtitle carry-forward are release-critical. Validate rollback idempotence and crash recovery without touching real source media.
validation_rung: Dedicated rerun transaction fault-injection suite across every boundary, restart/recovery tests, replacement and auto-destination smokes, strict change-packet gates, then representative disposable final-library media with subtitle sidecars.
prior_audit_relationship: No assembled current finding covered this replace-final ordering and rollback root cause; reproduced against the exact current hash with a disposable filesystem fixture.

title: ffprobe dot-decimal durations are parsed using the process culture
observed_behavior: Both duration paths call the two-argument Double.TryParse overload, which uses CurrentCulture. ffprobe emits invariant dot-decimal text; under a comma-decimal culture such as de-DE, '123.456' is accepted as 123456 because the dot is interpreted as a thousands separator.
expected_invariant: All numeric text emitted by ffprobe/FFmpeg must be parsed with CultureInfo.InvariantCulture and an explicit floating-point number style so media duration, progress, and policy decisions are locale-independent.
root_cause: Native-tool output parsing relies on the ambient PowerShell/.NET culture instead of the tool's invariant serialization contract.
failure_scenario: On a comma-decimal Windows locale, a 123.456-second input is treated as 123456 seconds. Duration reports and primary identity evidence are wrong, while encode waste-guard sampling positions and projected size decisions can be distorted by three orders of magnitude.
evidence: media_probe_reports.ps1 line 16 and encode_size_guard.ps1 line 160 use [double]::TryParse(text,[ref]) without culture or NumberStyles.
A current synthetic de-DE parse of ffprobe text '123.456' returned Ok=true and Parsed=123456.0.
The same ambient-culture pattern also exists in ffmpeg progress parsing, indicating the issue is a shared native-output parsing convention rather than malformed input.
affected_flows: encode waste-guard preflight sampling and size projection
existing_safeguards: Nonzero ffprobe exit and nonpositive duration results fail closed or skip preflight.
Probe calls are bounded by timeouts.
safeguard_gap: TryParse succeeds with a plausible but catastrophically wrong value, so existing failure checks cannot detect the locale misinterpretation.
tests_present: Media probe, encode size-guard inspection, and processing tests cover control flow on the default test culture.
tests_missing: Table-driven invariant numeric parsing under en-US, de-DE, fr-FR, and a custom comma-decimal culture
End-to-end waste-guard fixture proving identical decisions across cultures
recommended_remediation: Centralize native-tool floating-point parsing with Double.TryParse(value, NumberStyles.Float, CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, out result), reject nonfinite values, and migrate every ffprobe/FFmpeg numeric-output consumer to it.
remediation_risk: Medium: tightening numeric styles can expose previously tolerated malformed or thousands-formatted text. Inventory all native numeric parsers and add locale matrix tests before changing policy thresholds.
validation_rung: Focused PowerShell unit tests under multiple CurrentCulture values, probe and encode-size-guard checks, progress parser parity tests, and a synthetic ffprobe-output integration; real media is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: No assembled current finding covered invariant-culture native duration parsing; reproduced against the exact current hashes.

title: The first completed-job append after an abandoned mutex is silently dropped
observed_behavior: WaitOne throws AbandonedMutexException when a prior writer dies while holding the named completed-jobs mutex. The append helper catches it only in the generic outer catch, logs a warning, returns false, and writes no line even though the current thread owns the recovered mutex.
expected_invariant: A writer that acquires an abandoned named mutex must treat ownership as acquired, perform the append under the lock, and release it; a successfully published output should not lose its first completion-mirror entry solely because a previous writer terminated.
root_cause: Write-RerunJsonLineAppend lacks the AbandonedMutexException recovery branch already implemented by Write-RerunManifest for the adjacent named-mutex pattern.
failure_scenario: A rerun process terminates while holding the completed-jobs lock. The next successful publication obtains the abandoned mutex exception, drops its completion entry, and only emits a warning; later reconciliation or reporting sees final media/sidecar without the expected completed-jobs mirror row.
evidence: entry_support.ps1 lines 1017-1025 calls WaitOne inside the generic try/catch and returns false on every exception.
Write-RerunManifest lines 900-904 in the same file catches AbandonedMutexException and sets acquired=true.
A current C# thread-assisted synthetic abandoned-mutex fixture returned Written=false and FileExists=false on the first append.
affected_flows: completed manifest reporting and backfill evidence
existing_safeguards: The named mutex serializes normal concurrent appends.
Append failure is surfaced as a warning and the plan records completed_manifest_append='append_failed'.
The canonical sidecar remains the primary per-output evidence.
safeguard_gap: The warning does not repair the missing mirror entry, and the helper discards valid lock ownership supplied by .NET after abandonment.
tests_present: Rerun recovery and completed-manifest backfill checks cover normal completion evidence; manifest writer code covers abandoned mutex recovery for a different helper.
tests_missing: Concurrent append plus process/thread termination test
Recovery/backfill assertion for append_failed after successful publication
recommended_remediation: Catch AbandonedMutexException around WaitOne, set acquired=true, continue the append, and add focused abandoned/concurrent writer tests. Preserve false returns for genuine timeout or I/O failure.
remediation_risk: Low: the .NET exception conveys ownership, but cleanup must release only when ownership was obtained and the JSONL append must remain one encoded line.
validation_rung: Focused rerun entry-support concurrency tests, recovery and completed-manifest backfill checks; no real media is required.
prior_audit_relationship: No assembled current finding covered abandoned completed-jobs mutex ownership; reproduced against the exact current hash.

title: Setup normalizes a valid drive root into a drive-relative path
observed_behavior: Normalize-UserPath calls GetFullPath and then unconditionally trims trailing directory separators. For a Windows volume root such as C:\, this returns C:, which is drive-relative and resolves against that drive's current directory rather than the filesystem root.
expected_invariant: Path normalization must preserve root semantics for volume roots and UNC share roots; every persisted source, output, local, or config path must remain fully qualified and unambiguous.
root_cause: The normalizer treats a root separator as cosmetic trailing syntax instead of part of the canonical root returned by Path.GetPathRoot.
failure_scenario: An operator intentionally configures a whole volume root for SourceMovies, SourceTV, Outsource, LocalBase, or ConfigPath. Setup writes C: into the generated configuration, and later processes target the drive's ambient current directory instead of C:\.
evidence: Setup-MediaPipeline.ps1 lines 103-109 applies TrimEnd('\\','/') to every GetFullPath result and fallback.
An AST-extracted current function call with Input='C:\\' returned Normalized='C:', InputIsRoot=true, and NormalizedIsFullyQualified=false.
The setup entrypoint exposes source, output, local-base, and config paths to this helper and has no drive-root regression test.
affected_flows: subsequent path-boundary and free-space checks consuming persisted configuration
existing_safeguards: Relative inputs are converted through GetFullPath.
UNC inputs avoid GetFullPath and retain their leading share marker.
Runtime path validation checks several boundary relationships.
safeguard_gap: A syntactically valid fully qualified input is made ambiguous before persistence; downstream validation may then evaluate a resolved drive-current-directory path rather than the operator's root intent.
tests_present: Config-key, runtime-config, and path-boundary suites cover ordinary directory paths but no Setup-MediaPipeline drive-root normalization case was found.
tests_missing: Drive-root cases for every supported volume letter
Assertion that every persisted setup path is fully qualified
recommended_remediation: After GetFullPath, compare the result with Path.GetPathRoot and preserve the root separator when they are equal; normalize UNC roots similarly and reject any result that is not fully qualified before writing configuration.
remediation_risk: Medium: path normalization feeds high-risk source/output boundaries. Preserve existing nonroot canonicalization and validate migration of already-written drive-relative values without guessing operator intent.
validation_rung: Focused setup path-normalization tests, config/runtime resolution and path-boundary checks, plus a disposable volume-root dry run; no media mutation or representative media is required.
prior_audit_relationship: No assembled current finding covered drive-root trimming in the setup entrypoint; reproduced against the exact current hash.
